checks.source_locations: Publisher PDF pp.13,16,24-25; Definition4.1, Lemma4.7, Corollary4.8 and proof of Theorem2.6
checks.reason: With V_k=Leb(B1), the two radial integrals are k V_k[epsilon^-2alpha integral_0^epsilon r^(alpha-1)dr + integral_epsilon^infinity r^(-alpha-1)dr]=2k V_k epsilon^-alpha/alpha. The displayed L=2V_k omits k. Taking k=2, alpha=1/4, epsilon=1 gives 16pi rather than 8pi; E(delta_x)=U(0) for an admissible initial Dirac probability measure, so the specified ceiling is genuinely false within the operative range.

Replacing L by 2kV_k changes only the finite C''_alpha. Iteration E_n<=max(lambda^n C''_alpha epsilon^-alpha,Ctilde) with epsilon=lambda^(n/alpha) gives the same shrinking cutoff kappa=lambda^(1/alpha) and Holder exponent alpha/2; only the finite ball-mass prefactor changes. This directly verifies why the local constant error does not refute the main regularity conclusions.

checks.source_locations: Publisher PDF p.27 / printed1063, Lemma6.6; Definition4.1 on p.13
checks.reason: The source quantifier is all alpha,epsilon>0. For k=1,alpha=3,epsilon=1, phi(r)=r below1 and r^-2 above1. Independent piecewise integration gives U(1)=2(3/2-2log2)+2(log2-1/2)+1/6=13/6-2log2, and U(2)=2(1/3-log3/4)+2(log(3/2)-1/3)+2(1-log2)=2+3log3/2-4log2. Hence U(2)-U(1)=log(27/16)/2-1/6>11/43-1/6=23/258>0. The bound uses log x>2(x-1)/(x+1) for x>1; numeric values 0.7803723055 and0.8753297108 are only corroboration.

checks.source_locations: Publisher PDF pp.16 and27; Proposition4.6 operative alpha range
checks.reason: The counterexample satisfies every printed positivity condition and phi is square integrable. The proof's unspoken radial non-increase fails when alpha>k. Restricting to 0<alpha<=k makes phi radial non-increasing, so its positive layer-cake decomposition into balls and the intersection-volume argument validate convolution monotonicity. The main proof already uses 0<alpha<1/2, contained in that sufficient repaired range for positive integer k. No maximal valid range or failure of the main theorem is claimed.
